notes.text: Chullin 95b names Rav’s son-in-law Hanan without a patronymic. The earlier dossiers and Chullin 60b show why Heilprin distinguishes Hanan bar Abba from Hanan bar Rava. The printed alternate genealogies remain attributed.

Yuhasin p. 102 supplies the Abbahu report from R. Ishmael Hakhamon. The cited Talmudic episode remains unlocated. Shabbat supplies the eulogy dialogue, while the unspecific Moed Katan parallel remains open.

Tosafot on Keritot names Rava bar Rav Hanan in the “tarda” exchange, the digital Gemara names Rabbah bar bar Hana, and Rashi gives the two glosses. The other folios preserve Rava/Rabbah, Hanan/Hanin, and Hana separately.
